raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43150.

The streaming `Qwen3CoderDetector` closes a call's arguments object only on `</function>`. When the model ends the call with `</tool_call>` but omits `</function>`, the streamed `arguments` stop mid-object; when `</parameter>` is missing too, the parameter is never emitted. `detect_and_parse` returns `{"days": 0}` for both, so the same output succeeds or fails depending only on `stream`. Current main, character-by-character:

```
...<parameter=days>\n0\n</parameter>\n</tool_call>   streamed: '{"days": 0'
...<parameter=days>\n0\n</tool_call>                 streamed: ''
```

## Modifications

- At `</tool_call>`, if a function is still open, emit the closing `}` (and the opening `{` for a call without parameters).
- Override `finish()`, which runs once when the stream ends. No `</parameter>` can arrive any more, so a parameter that is still open ends at `</tool_call>`, which is how `detect_and_parse` reads it.
- `</tool_call>` ends a parameter only at stream end. This differs from the diff suggested in the issue and from the closed #43467, which make it an unconditional terminator. Mid-stream, `</tool_call>` can be literal text in a value that a later `</parameter>` closes, for example a coding agent writing parser code. Main streams that case correctly today; with the unconditional terminator it becomes invalid JSON plus leaked content:

  ```
  <parameter=content>\nprint("</tool_call>")\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>
  main:                     {"content": "print(\"</tool_call>\")"}
  unconditional terminator: {"content": "print(\""}}   and content text ")\n</parameter>\n\n"
  ```

  A second test pins this down.

Related, not changed here:

- #45244 (open) makes a stray `</function>` after a closed call inert. It changes the `</function>` branch, this PR changes the `</tool_call>` branch and the parameter scan, so the two compose.
- The shape from the issue thread where the model omits both `</function>` and `</tool_call>` and opens the next call directly is not covered: `detect_and_parse` merges those two calls as well, so it needs a one-shot change too.

## Accuracy Tests

Parser-only change; no model-forward or kernel code is touched.

Local CPU run, Python 3.12:

- `test_function_call_parser.py -k Qwen3Coder`: 19 passed.
- `test_streaming_closes_arguments_when_function_end_omitted` covers the two shapes from the issue and a call with no parameters; all three subcases fail on main and pass here. `test_streaming_keeps_tool_call_end_inside_parameter_value` passes on main and here, and fails when `</tool_call>` is made an unconditional terminator.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/` plus `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_{chat,responses,responses_stream}.py`: 867 passed, no new failures compared with main. The 18 cases that fail in my environment fail the same way on main; they need packages that only ship Linux/macOS wheels (`deepseek-recipe`, `tml-renderers`, `uvloop`).
- isort, `ruff check` (pre-commit selection), `ruff format --check` and codespell are clean on the changed files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: mid-stream the parameter scan only adds a flag check; the extra `str.find` runs only inside `finish()`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable to a parser-only change.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -57,6 +57,7 @@ def __init__(self):
 
         # Initialize attributes that were missing in the original PR
         self.current_func_name: Optional[str] = None
+        self._stream_ended: bool = False
 
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         return self.tool_call_start_token in text
@@ -315,10 +316,18 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
                     # 1. [Normal] Encounter </parameter>
                     # 2. [Abnormal] Encounter next <parameter=
                     # 3. [Abnormal] Encounter </function>
+                    # 4. [Abnormal] Encounter </tool_call>, once the stream has ended
                     # So we need to find the smallest one as the parameter end position.
                     cand_end_param = rest_of_slice.find(self.parameter_end_token)
                     cand_next_param = rest_of_slice.find(self.parameter_prefix)
                     cand_end_func = rest_of_slice.find(self.function_end_token)
+                    # Mid-stream, </tool_call> may be literal text in a value that a
+                    # later </parameter> closes.
+                    cand_end_tool = (
+                        rest_of_slice.find(self.tool_call_end_token)
+                        if self._stream_ended
+                        else -1
+                    )
 
                     candidates = []
                     if cand_end_param != -1:
@@ -329,6 +338,8 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
                         candidates.append((cand_next_param, 0))
                     if cand_end_func != -1:
                         candidates.append((cand_end_func, 0))
+                    if cand_end_tool != -1:
+                        candidates.append((cand_end_tool, 0))
 
                     if candidates:
                         best_cand = min(candidates, key=lambda x: x[0])
@@ -407,6 +418,20 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
             # 5. Tool Call End: </tool_call>
             # -------------------------------------------------------
             if current_slice.startswith(self.tool_call_end_token):
+                if self.current_func_name is not None:
+                    # The model omitted </function>; close the arguments object
+                    # anyway, as detect_and_parse does.
+                    if not self.json_started:
+                        calls.append(
+                            ToolCallItem(
+                                tool_index=self.current_tool_id, parameters="{"
+                            )
+                        )
+                        self.json_started = True
+                    calls.append(
+                        ToolCallItem(tool_index=self.current_tool_id, parameters="}")
+                    )
+                    self.current_func_name = None
                 self.parsed_pos += len(self.tool_call_end_token)
                 self.is_inside_tool_call = False  # [FIX] Exit tool call region
                 continue
@@ -473,6 +498,12 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         normal_text = "".join(normal_text_chunks) if normal_text_chunks else ""
         return StreamingParseResult(calls=calls, normal_text=normal_text)
 
+    def finish(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult:
+        # No </parameter> can arrive any more, so a parameter still open ends at
+        # </tool_call>, as detect_and_parse reads it.
+        self._stream_ended = True
+        return self.parse_streaming_increment("", tools)
+
     def supports_structural_tag(self) -> bool:
         return True

@@ -2507,6 +2507,44 @@ def test_streaming_with_text_and_tool(self):
         self.assertTrue(full_text.startswith("Let me"))
         self.assertGreater(len(all_calls), 0)
 
+    def _stream_arguments(self, text):
+        detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+        results = [detector.parse_streaming_increment(ch, self.tools) for ch in text]
+        results.append(detector.finish(self.tools))
+        return "".join(
+            call.parameters
+            for result in results
+            for call in result.calls
+            if call.parameters
+        )
+
+    def test_streaming_closes_arguments_when_function_end_omitted(self):
+        """A call closed by </tool_call> without </function> must still stream
+        complete arguments, the same JSON as detect_and_parse."""
+        head = "<tool_call>\n<function=get_current_weather>\n"
+        cases = [
+            (head + "<parameter=days>\n0\n</parameter>\n</tool_call>", {"days": 0}),
+            (head + "<parameter=days>\n0\n</tool_call>", {"days": 0}),
+            (head + "</tool_call>", {}),
+        ]
+        for text, expected_args in cases:
+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                streamed = self._stream_arguments(text)
+                one_shot = self.detector.detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+                self.assertEqual(streamed, one_shot.calls[0].parameters)
+                self.assertEqual(json.loads(streamed), expected_args)
+
+    def test_streaming_keeps_tool_call_end_inside_parameter_value(self):
+        """A </tool_call> inside a value that </parameter> closes later is value
+        text; it must not end the parameter or the call."""
+        text = (
+            "<tool_call>\n<function=get_current_weather>\n"
+            "<parameter=location>\na</tool_call>b\n</parameter>\n"
+            "</function>\n</tool_call>"
+        )
+        streamed = self._stream_arguments(text)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(streamed), {"location": "a</tool_call>b"})
+
     # ==================== Parameter Type Tests ====================
 
     def test_integer_parameter_conversion(self):
